clue.text: Sergeant major, breaking phone, becomes gloomy

indicators.note: something breaking into another thing gets inside it, splitting it apart

parts.note: to dial is to phone someone
standard abbreviation for sergeant major

explanation.surface: A sergeant major barks into someone's phone call and the mood turns gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phone' is a verb here, the act of ringing a number, not the handset.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal and gloomy are synonyms describing a depressing, cheerless mood or outlook.

clue.text: Duke won't now broadcast in city centre

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn about

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A duke refuses to appear on radio or television in the city centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Downtown is the American term for a city's central business district, its city centre.

clue.text: Runner, representative to cut corners

parts.note: a ski is a runner, like those on a sledge
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: An athlete and a politician are both accused of taking shortcuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is the long blade a sledge slides on.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise by spending too little effort or money, which is what cutting corners means.

clue.text: Conductor losing son in a South American country

indicators.note: losing means letting go of something, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Sir Malcolm Sargent was a famous British conductor
S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An orchestra conductor's son goes missing in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Malcolm Sargent was a well-known British conductor of the mid-twentieth century, best remembered for the Proms.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in the south of the American continent, so it is a South American country.

clue.text: Teach group to make a model railway

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A class is taught how to build a model railway together.
explanation.definitionFit: A train set is a toy or hobby layout of track and engines, which is a model railway.

clue.text: Firework, too large to be brought into court!

indicators.note: something brought into a place ends up inside it

parts.note: to romance someone is to court or woo them
too and and both mean also
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A firework too big to be allowed into a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court, but it is the verb meaning to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman candle is a firework that shoots out a series of flaming balls from a tube.

clue.text: I prosecute after second matter

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the order they are written

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
to sue is to take legal action against someone

explanation.surface: Someone vows to prosecute after a second matter arises.
explanation.walkthrough: I comes first, then SUE is placed after S.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a topic or point in question, so it is a matter under discussion.

clue.text: Clever character produces a piece of plastic that stores data

definitions.text: a piece of plastic that stores data

parts.note: smart means clever
a card is an amusing or eccentric character

explanation.surface: A clever person creates a plastic data card.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart card is a plastic card with an embedded chip holding information, used for payments or access.

clue.text: Testing hearing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: difficult or annoying, putting patience to the test

definitions.note: noun; the answer is used as a verbal noun, the trying of a case
definitions.meaning: second meaning: judging a case in court

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a hearing test; each is a separate sense of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying describes something taxing to endure, and a court trying a case is conducting its hearing.

clue.text: Complain in western type of joint

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for western
a hinge is a kind of joint, on a door or in the body

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a joint, perhaps a sore knee, in Western style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but it only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To whinge is a British informal verb meaning to moan or grumble persistently, so it matches complain.

clue.text: Eastern girl, a really heartless spy

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
a miss is a girl or young woman
taken as written

indicators.note: a word with no heart has its middle removed, leaving just its two ends

parts.note: only the first and last letters of really are kept

explanation.surface: A girl from the East is described as a heartless spy, like a femme fatale in a thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an agent sent on a mission, which can include a secret agent or spy.

clue.text: Type of cricket clue with dash

parts.note: a tip is a hint or clue
with and and both mean together with
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter describes a cricket-themed crossword clue that contains a dash.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is a bat-and-ball game; tip-and-run is an informal version in which the batter must run whenever the ball is hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-and-run is a recognised informal variety of the game, so it is a kind of cricket.

clue.text: Mostly recreation, in travelling funfairs, for urchins

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter goes
one thing in another sits inside it
things travelling are on the move, so these letters shift position

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
a game is recreation; its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Ragged children enjoy some fun at travelling fairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted piece lands after the first two letters of the rearranged fairground word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragamuffins are scruffy, ragged children, the same as street urchins.

clue.text: Scoffed at in course of poetic evening

indicators.note: something happening in the course of a period sits within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even, meaning evening
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked during an evening of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed at' reads as one phrase meaning mocked, but the definition is just 'Scoffed', in its sense of gobbled; 'at' goes inside E'EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is British slang for eating it greedily, so scoffed matches the past participle eaten.

clue.text: Argument over supremo with excellent liquid assets

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a noisy argument
a king is the supreme ruler
capital is a dated British exclamation meaning excellent

explanation.surface: A dispute with a boss over company finances that are in excellent shape.
explanation.walkthrough: In a dated British exclamation, 'Capital!' means splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Working capital is the money a business has readily available for day-to-day operations, its liquid assets.

clue.text: As good as gold? Not quite, us!

definitions.text: As good as gold? Not quite, us!

parts.note: surface reading: the phrase for a well-behaved child
setter's reading: competitors speaking who just missed the gold medal and took silver

explanation.walkthrough: 'As good as gold' is an idiom for good behaviour; the clue reads it as a medal ranking, voiced by those placed second.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners-up are competitors who finish just behind the winner, so they were nearly but not quite gold medallists.

clue.text: Suffering from how poor performers perform?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in a bad state of health or condition
second meaning, taken literally: performing badly

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being ill or troubled is read literally as a manner of performing, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a bad way is an idiom for being ill, distressed or in serious trouble.

clue.text: Emphasised editor is under pressure

indicators.note: in a down answer, under places one piece below, so it is written after

parts.note: stress is pressure or strain
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is feeling the strain and stresses the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is under pressure' reads as one phrase, but 'under' places ED beneath STRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a word or point is to give it emphasis, so stressed means emphasised.

clue.text: Gaming machine in dated bar — endless money involved

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter
involved means tangled and complicated, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
money without its last letter

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned pub has a gambling machine swallowing customers' cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' looks like a link but is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-armed bandit is the slang name for a slot machine, worked by a single lever and taking players' money.

clue.text: Up-to-the-minute intelligence prior to strike

indicators.note: prior to puts the first piece ahead of the second in reading order

parts.note: wit is mental sharpness or intelligence
to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: Fresh intelligence arrives just before a military strike.
explanation.definitionFit: With-it is informal for fashionable and current, so it means up-to-the-minute.

clue.text: Perfect suggestion by learner driver

parts.note: an idea is a suggestion or proposal
L is the learner plate shown on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner driver offers a perfect suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless or exactly as wished, a synonym of perfect.

clue.text: One supplying eggs for plate?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hen that lays
second meaning: a thin sheet or coating, as in a plate of metal

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests eggs served on a plate, but plate is a thin flat sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer is a laying hen, and also a thin covering stratum, the sense of plate in metal plating.

clue.text: Tested public opinion, as aviator did?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: floated an idea to see how people would react
second meaning, taken literally: what someone in the air with a kite did

explanation.surface: A pollster's work is compared to a pilot's.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second reading is playful: the idiom is taken literally as an aerial activity.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly a kite is an idiom for releasing a proposal to gauge reaction before committing to it.

clue.text: Mental picture of him, a goalkeeper

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the letters come from the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: Someone forms a mental picture of a goalkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from inside him through a into goalkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychoanalysis an imago is an idealised mental image of a person, such as a parent.

clue.text: It's fishy, comic's temper tantrum

indicators.note: something comic is absurd or ridiculous, suggesting the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone suspicious throws a tantrum while a comedian looks on.
explanation.definitionFit: A hissy fit is informal for an outburst of petulant anger, which is a temper tantrum.

clue.text: Clothes worn initially in pews

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: pews are church seats

indicators.note: initially points to the very first letter of the preceding word

parts.note: first letter of worn

explanation.surface: Churchgoers' clothing is noticed as they sit in the pews.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside SEATS: S-W-EATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweats is informal for a sweatsuit or tracksuit, loose casual clothing.

clue.text: High-ranking officials decorate section of orchestra

parts.note: to top a cake is to decorate it with something on top
the brass is the trumpet and horn section

explanation.surface: Senior officials decorate the brass section's music stands at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Top brass is an idiom for the senior people in charge, especially military commanders.

clue.text: 'Times'term, an outstanding example

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in two by three
a term is a word

explanation.surface: A term used by The Times newspaper is held up as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make Times look like the newspaper; it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A byword is a person or thing cited as the notable instance of some quality, a prime example.
